# Independent template review — reviewer one

Date: 2026-10-29. Repository identity: `aaaAlexanderaaa/template-project`.
Baseline HEAD: `fa01192f094585ff0c1aaa6942ac04e63a11983a`, plus the extensive
tracked and untracked working-tree changes already present. This review used
the actual working tree. `$REPOSITORY` means that checkout; `$PROBE_ROOT` means
this uniquely owned temporary observation directory. Disposable paths below
are normalized for possible publication.

## First verdict and current disposition

The unchanged first verdict is retained in `first-verdict.md`. It was written
before sending the parent a finding, receiving another review, or receiving a
producer response. The subsequent Git checkout probe confirms it; no finding
was withdrawn or broadened.

The template makes substantial progress toward the owner's goal. It now has a
coherent route from original intent through authority, complete activated
rules, task methods, actual effects and completion. Its practical layer covers
several useful task families, and its normal LF rule-delivery and recovery
paths work in this review. One reproduced P2 portability defect remains: CRLF
frontmatter prevents the new reader from delivering those rules. This bounded
review is complete; implementation and integration belong to the parent.

This is not assurance that every domain discipline is correct or that the
template has achieved durable independent adoption.

## Supplied context, independence and authority

Actual inherited context consisted of the system/developer/tool instructions,
the repository working agreement and environment supplied as a user message,
and the native review assignment. The brief at
`$BRIEF/2026-10-29-template-wide-review-brief.txt` supplied the original owner
goal and corrections as English renderings, with an explicit warning that
these were not verbatim English quotations. I did not receive the producing
conversation history, inspect other current workers' outputs, or read the
parent's synthesis. I did not inspect the coordination record because the
native assignment already established my read-only scope and concurrent work.

I therefore have a fresh review context relative to producing the work, with
repository instructions and substantial framing supplied. It is not an empty
context or an artifact-only consumer experiment. The declared identity is
Codex based on GPT-6; the exact backend model identifier is unavailable in this
context. No model diversity or independent acquisition of the supplied owner
history is claimed.

The selected method was `docs/guides/grill.md`, read in full. Before judgments,
I obtained the task-context core, governance core, execution risk/route/
completion, independence and delegation boundaries. The reader's actual
Experience concern was bound to
`docs/contracts/documentation-harness.md`, whose full body was read. I read
`docs-policy.toml` before interpreting checker coverage. I also inspected the
applicable adoption/learning rules before judging their entry route.

The assignment allowed read-only repository investigation, bounded local
checks and uniquely owned disposable probes. Repository files, Git state,
plans, policy and evidence were not edited. All Python probes used
`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. No network requests, neighboring project scripts,
unrelated private locations or additional agents were used.

## Finding F1 — P2: normal CRLF checkouts block rule delivery

State: `fact`, with a bounded portability `risk`.

Primary locator: `scripts/rule_reading.py:17` (LF-only opening delimiter) and
`scripts/rule_reading.py:19` (LF-only closing delimiter). The raw-byte caller is
`scripts/rule_reading.py:154` through line 158. The intended source-delivery
boundary is `docs/contracts/documentation-harness.md:249` through line 259.

Mechanism: `source()` reads bytes and decodes UTF-8 without newline
normalization, while `parse_frontmatter_text()` recognizes only literal
`---\n` and `\n---\n`. A CRLF Markdown document consequently reports
`missing frontmatter` even though its metadata and rule contents are unchanged.
The repository has no `.gitattributes` file imposing LF checkout for Markdown.

Observed effect: using the same five actual source files that define the
normal core closure, the LF copy delivered nine units and the final completion
marker. Converting only newline style to CRLF failed with exit 1, zero stdout
bytes and this error:

```text
read_rules: docs/contracts/development-discipline.md: missing frontmatter
```

A control retaining LF metadata while converting body lines to CRLF succeeds.
This isolates the metadata delimiters rather than rule text, source identity,
or general UTF-8/body handling. A second probe used an actual local Git index
with `core.autocrlf=true`, then `checkout-index` into a new temporary directory.
Git produced CRLF metadata and the reader failed identically. This is an
observed Git conversion on macOS, not a claim to have run Windows.

The affected person is an adopter or maintainer whose checkout uses CRLF.
The immediate impact is failure of `list`/`prepare` at metadata loading and no
prepared rules for the normal task route. The portable engineering template
thus transfers an avoidable failure into the exact rule-acquisition step meant
to prevent skipped requirements. Direct complete reading remains an authorized
fallback, so this is P2 rather than a total loss of capability. LF checkouts
and CRLF confined to rule bodies are unaffected. Incidence across real adopters
is unknown; accepting this risk assumes they enforce LF metadata themselves or
manually recover through direct reading.

Evidence: `newline_probe.py`, `newline-results.json`, `git_newline_probe.py`
and `git-newline-results.json`. Raw stdout/stderr from all three newline
variants are retained alongside them. These probes make copies under
`$PROBE_ROOT` and invoke the current repository reader. No repair was applied.
An optional repair direction is newline-tolerant metadata recognition while
retaining original bytes for digests and output; this suggestion is not part
of the verified result.

## Supported improvements and status of the owner's earlier concerns

| Concern from the supplied brief | Judgment and evidence | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| Global abstractions must not substitute for activated detailed rules | Solved at the observed source-routing boundary on LF input. `docs/README.md` distinguishes authority, applicability, unit scope, force and completion; preparation emits the full core and the bound non-graphical Experience owner. Digest recovery delivered every missing core part after tool-output truncation. | Delivery cannot establish understanding or application; the contract states this limit. F1 affects CRLF input. |
| Concrete SOPs should accompany high-level rules | Substantially improved. `project-operation.md:33` gives the request-to-result sequence and worked task decisions; the task CheatSheet supplies triggers, executable prompts, examples and useful results. Actual rule-reader commands and the documented recovery commands were usable in this review. | Reading the other recipes establishes their content and findability, not comparative effectiveness or successful execution of every recipe. |
| Mission and intended user change must survive task and metric translation | The current owners address the earlier mechanism directly. Development's outcome rule preserves original request and accepted interpretation; layered completion prevents examples from closing a broader goal; the SOP asks what remains after a step succeeds. | I did not observe a real product project sustain that discipline over time. |
| Give supported positive judgments and stop at a useful result | Current language-style, Grill and closure guidance explicitly permit a supported pass, name what works and give a sufficient stopping point. This review can state concrete gains rather than invent a defect quota. | Wording alone does not prove future agents will follow it. |
| Independent review and external use should reveal producer omissions | Review guidance leaves inspection open beyond the diff and preserves first judgments, actual inheritance, unique findings and consumer trials as distinct evidence. This assignment enabled a normal-use defect beyond ideal fixtures. | Same-source and possibly same-model dependence remain. The separate consumer trial is not this review's evidence. |
| Review is one concise method among many | Addressed in the observed artifact. The main collection includes diagnosis, inquiry, fallback, delivery, explanation, continuity, learning and simplification; review is a linked specialization. | No universal completeness or ranking of the collection is claimed. |
| Separate public-practice grounding, historical questions, rule-based design and implementer invention | The task CheatSheet's source section and question-starter labels distinguish these origins and preserve transformations. The prose explicitly separates attribution from effectiveness. | Public originals and private historical originals were not revalidated in this review. I credit the visible distinction, not the fidelity or effectiveness of every transfer. |

The existing overdue adoption-review promise remains visible at
`docs/contracts/agent-execution-discipline.md:584`. The contract's acceptance
section and README already describe external effectiveness as unproved. The
checker reported the promise as advisory under the actual policy. I did not
manufacture a second finding from an openly declared evidence gap; neither a
fixture pass nor this one-off review closes a real-project adoption claim.

## Commands, probes and outcomes

The exact review baseline, source hashes, byte counts and reading scopes are
in `source-identities.json`; the core and Experience manifests retain unit and
whole-file digests. Inspection included root entrypoints, rule owners, actual
guides, selected reusable templates, reader implementation and reader tests.
The file is explicit about excerpts versus whole-source reading.

| Command or observation | Actual result |
|---|---|
| `git status --short`; `git rev-parse HEAD`; `git remote -v` | Existing dirty tree, expected HEAD and template origin; no repository mutations by this reviewer. Final status retained. |
| `python3 --version` | Python 3.14.2, satisfying the 3.11-or-newer requirement. A second interpreter was not used. |
| `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 scripts/read_rules.py list` | Current concern routing emitted successfully. |
| `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 scripts/read_rules.py prepare` | Nine-unit core delivered by CLI; initial tool display was truncated. The original LF-copy transcript is 97,685 bytes and ends `READING COMPLETE units=9`. |
| `read --unit docs/contracts/development-discipline.md#development-core --digest <manifest-file-digest> --part N --part-size 12000`, N = 1–4 | All four parts obtained, each with current file digest and `PART COMPLETE`. |
| Equivalent `read` for `governance-core`, N = 1–3 | All three parts obtained with completion markers. |
| `prepare --concern experience --owner experience=docs/contracts/documentation-harness.md` | Exit 0; ten-unit closure and `READING COMPLETE units=10`, with the actual CLI owner and no required frontend unit. Full relevant bodies were retained/read. |
| `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` | Exit 0; 169 tests passed in 42.949 seconds. Output: `unit-tests.txt`. The suite includes actual-template relocation/default-role/domain-closure cases, whose source was inspected. |
| `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 scripts/check_docs.py` | Exit 0; 65 canonical documents, 16 templates, full profile, adopted stage; one advisory for the overdue promise. Output: `docs-check.txt`. Template mode contains no product implementation. |
| `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $PROBE_ROOT/newline_probe.py` | LF pass; complete CRLF metadata fail; LF metadata with CRLF body pass. See F1. |
| `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $PROBE_ROOT/git_newline_probe.py` | Actual Git checkout conversion produced the same failing boundary. See F1. |
| `git diff --check` | Exit 0, no whitespace-error output. |

The comparisons held source content, authority, closure, interpreter and
reader implementation fixed while varying newline representation. The
Git-generated counterexample held the underlying source origin fixed too;
it corroborates the transformation mechanism, not independent source truth.
All outputs were local. Tests and the checker were run once each; successful
results were not repeatedly rerun without a changed condition.

## Scope, unresolved judgments and stop basis

This was one substantive bounded whole-project review, using its own route
rather than a selected diff. It combined entrypoint reading, current-authority
inspection, normal CLI use, output-limit recovery, the actual infrastructure
suite and a meaningful portability countercase. The finding has an exact
mechanism, normal-use reproduction and an unaffected control; further blind
search was unlikely to improve that immediate judgment enough to justify
extending this assignment.

The review did not perform a full semantic audit of every domain, raw historical
source, checker branch or target engineering-judgment proposal. It did not
trial a production migration, unattended autonomous operation, every practical
recipe, or a real adopter's long-term owner-attention cost. Those claims remain
unknown here. The repository's own honest limits should be preserved in any
synthesis. The parent's integration should evaluate F1 against the current
source identities and keep this review's positive conclusions at their stated
scope.

# Independent template review — reviewer two

## Verdict and preserved first judgment

The working tree materially improves the engineering template. Its task SOP, practical task moves, question starters, and review method provide usable actions while keeping intent, authority, evidence, and completion distinct. The normal copied-backend-contract route works. Three consequential P2 issues remain in rule delivery and ordinary adoption paths. The existing owners are sufficient places to address them.

My first independent verdict is retained unchanged in `first-verdict.md` (SHA-256 `67744a587e6540de9a979889ddf458fb2333deca1a6168c6d6bb4994ee564484`). It already supported the practical improvements and the root-product detection finding. The time-unit and minimal-profile findings were added after further source inspection and probes; no other review or producer defense was received. No original finding was retracted or silently rewritten. The contract reading before that verdict included embedded historical acceptance evidence; the first-verdict reference to historical producer reports means separate evidence reports, which I did not open.

This is one substantive bounded review, not assurance that every instruction, domain, project layout, or future workflow is effective.

## Actual supplied context and independence

The runtime supplied the task message, the English review brief, repository AGENTS instructions, the repository path and environment, general agent instructions, the available skills/tools catalog, and the collaboration tool environment. I did not receive the producing conversation's turns, a personal-context entrypoint, the executor's detailed reasoning, another current reviewer's result, or the integration owner's synthesis. The brief supplies English renderings of owner goals and corrections; I treat them as the assigned account, not verbatim English owner quotations.

This was a separate native agent context. That fact does not establish an empty environment or a different model. The precise deployed model identifier, whether it differs from the other reviewers' models, and hidden runtime/model dependencies are not exposed to me. The runtime describes the assistant as based on GPT-6; I did not invent a more specific model identity.

I did not open the current coordination record or other current worker outputs. Repository-wide checker/tests necessarily traverse canonical documents mechanically; they did not return the coordination record's contents. Disposable probe copies explicitly excluded `docs/evidence/2026-10-29-template-wide-review.md`. No further agents were spawned, no external service was consulted, and no private history was disclosed.

## Scope and inspection route

Baseline: actual working tree on HEAD `fa01192f094585ff0c1aaa6942ac04e63a11983a`, including the tracked edits and relevant untracked rules/guides/scripts/tests. I did not restrict inspection to a commit diff.

I selected Grill as the review method and read it in full, then examined:

- normal startup and task selection through README, the task-context core, contributor instructions, project operation, and the practical task/review guidance;
- current authority for independence, delegation, adoption scope, documentation enforcement, and time-policy recovery before judging those boundaries;
- the complete reader implementation, its tests, and the checker's relevant metadata, traversal, adoption, template, and reading-declaration code;
- actual supplied templates and their documented relocation;
- a relevant successful copy, a product-layout countercase, time versus demonstration reading, and the documented minimal-profile use.

Full obtained text includes `docs/README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the complete development and governance core units, the documentation-harness contract, the foundational-runtime operative material through Acceptance evidence, Grill, project operation, the task CheatSheet, question starters, review CheatSheet, research, the template README, generic/backend/cross-stack templates, both reader source files, and `tests/test_read_rules.py`. Adoption, execution, onboarding, and checker tests were inspected at the relevant sections described above. The data-analysis contract was inventoried by metadata/headings, not semantically reviewed. The autonomous-operation runtime and target engineering-judgment method were not independently exercised.

Source identities are retained in `snapshot-identities.json` and the reader manifests. `source-scope.json` distinguishes model-inspected paths from files only copied or mechanically checked. The copied tree is a fixture, not an independent real project. All snapshots were removed after probes. `review-integrity.json` reports no changed source-file digest among the captured baseline files.

## Consequential findings

### F1 — P2 — Time preparation reports completion without an applicable recovery rule

State: `fact` for missing delivery; `risk` for the induced decision gap. Primary locators: `docs/contracts/foundational-runtime-discipline.md:225` and `docs/contracts/foundational-runtime-discipline.md:327-330`. The current reading owner is `docs/contracts/documentation-harness.md`, Complete rule delivery; task context requires complete applicable units including dependencies and exceptions.

The Time and calendar unit closes at line 225. The same current contract later requires a human data-risk decision if persisted values were naive or rewritten by a timezone change. That recovery condition is outside the unit, and the unit declares no reading dependency carrying it.

Observed command:

```text
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 scripts/read_rules.py prepare --concern time-and-calendar
```

It exits 0, delivers the global core plus `foundational-runtime-discipline.md#time`, and ends `READING COMPLETE units=10`. Its delivered text does not contain that data-risk condition. As a useful countercase, preparing Demonstration data selects the whole-document fallback and does contain it. The missing text is thus not unavailable or stale; the declared time boundary excludes it.

Mechanism and consequence: a consumer following the advertised selected-unit path can correctly obtain every emitted unit while missing a binding condition relevant to repairing stored timestamps. This directly leaves part of the owner's complete-activated-rule goal unmet. A manifest and syntactically complete unit cannot establish semantic completeness.

Impact is on implementers and owners of an affected time-data repair; mishandled historical values could have durable consequences. No data repair was performed, no actual harm or frequency was measured, and the test does not show that an agent will necessarily make the wrong choice: other current rules can still route uncertainty to the owner. The problem does not arise if the worker separately reads the whole runtime contract or a project owner explicitly carries the condition. Accepting this delivery gap assumes those additional routes will be used. Priority is P2 because the omission is reproducible and consequential, with no observed active production incident.

Evidence: `reader-probe-results.json`, `time-prepare.txt`, `demo-prepare.txt`.

### F2 — P2 — The root-file exception hides an ordinary root-only application

State: `fact` for the checker behavior; `risk` for the lost adoption guard. Primary locator: `scripts/check_docs.py:1518-1520`. Related current text: `docs/contracts/documentation-harness.md`, Enforcement stage and managed scope; `docs/contracts/project-adoption.md:431-443`; `README.md:139-145`.

The outside-source-root scan skips every file directly at repository root. That exception was designed for build/tool configuration, but it also classifies an ordinary `main.py` application out of the detection surface.

In a disposable copy with the shipped adopted stage and `source_roots = ["src"]`:

1. Unchanged template: checker exits 0.
2. Add a root `main.py` containing an application entrypoint: checker still exits 0 with the same findings, while architecture remains unconfigured and no product contract exists.
3. Move the exact source to `app/main.py`: checker exits 1 and names the unclaimed source path.

Mechanism and consequence: the current exception equates repository position with tooling identity. A root-only application's entire source can remain invisible to the guard that otherwise catches an empty governed file set. This is a design defect in the exception rather than a failure to implement the explicit exception: the current harness prose also exempts root files. It conflicts with the broader portable-adoption promise that code outside declared source roots is reported instead of passed silently.

Impact is on small-project adopters using a common single-file layout and on maintainers who rely on the scope guard. The magnitude is the whole root-only application's missing detection, not a measured population of adopters. Existing obligations to inspect architecture and establish contracts still bind; a green checker never grants implementation authority. The problem does not arise for correctly configured directory source roots or a deliberately configured root scope. I did not test the usability of `source_roots = ["."]`, and do not claim root files are impossible to govern. Accepting this gap assumes manual inventory catches it or every adopter configures/moves root application code despite the published blanket exemption.

Evidence: `probe-results.json`, `baseline.txt`, `root-product.txt`, `directory-product.txt`. Product text was never executed. The copy omitted Git metadata, so this is checker-boundary evidence, not a finished adoption.

### F3 — P2 — The documented minimal adoption breaks the prescribed test/CI route

State: `fact` for local validation failure; `risk` for downstream delivery and maintenance cost. Primary locators: `tests/test_read_rules.py:64-71` and `tests/test_read_rules.py:348-379`; related mechanism in `tests/test_check_docs.py:34-48` and `tests/test_check_docs.py:877-918`. The public promises are `README.md:133-135`, `tests/README.md:23-31`, and `templates/ci/docs-check.example.yml:25`.

The README says a minimal project can delete standard/full templates. Tests guidance tells adopters to keep the fixture suite, and the example per-change CI runs the full unittest command. The tests use the adopter's live tree as their fixture baseline, unconditionally read higher-profile templates, and assume the original policy still contains `profile = "full"`.

I copied the current tree, changed only its selected profile to minimal, and deleted exactly the templates declared in the standard and full tiers. Results:

```text
python3 scripts/check_docs.py
  exit 0; 4 templates, profile minimal; dropped-template references advisory
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
  exit 1; 169 tests; 8 failures and 18 errors
```

The checker-only profile case passes while the actual prescribed validation route fails. A small adopter has to retain optional material, adapt the inherited infrastructure suite, or abandon the supplied CI step; the normal path does not explain that work.

Impact is on every adopter combining the documented trimming path with the retained suite/CI command. It causes deterministic local validation failure in this trial and consumes maintainer attention; hosted GitHub CI was not run. The issue does not affect the unchanged full template or a downstream project that has intentionally replaced/adapted the suite. Accepting it assumes adopters understand that extra fixture maintenance despite the current keep-the-suite guidance. This is P2 portability work, not a need for a new approval gate.

Evidence: `minimal-probe-results.json`, `minimal-check.normalized.txt`, `minimal-tests.normalized.txt`, and the actual reproduction script `minimal-probe.py`. Raw output stays beside those files outside the repository.

| Abstractions without concrete SOPs | Improved substantially. Project operation gives a request-to-result sequence and worked task decisions. The task CheatSheet supplies executable moves for diagnosis, inquiry, delivery, explanation, continuity, learning, and simplification. This reviewer could choose relevant probes without inventing another process. | This single review is no comparative effectiveness study or real adopter sample. |
| Global guidance skipping detailed requirements | Partly improved. Default preparation delivers identifiable core bodies; copied backend preparation obtains the backend unit through the actual relocated template. Digest-checked development/governance recovery succeeds. F1 leaves a real activated-rule omission. | Source delivery does not prove an executor applied each rule. |
| Preserving purpose through task, acceptance, and result | The current owners explicitly compare original request, accepted interpretation, actual effects, and named stopping point. Worked decisions distinguish a lookup, a bounded link repair, a broad template improvement, a timeout defect, and analytical explanation. | These instructions are present and intelligible; future work selection and owner benefit were not measured. |
| Supported positive judgments | Current language guidance and Grill explicitly allow a supported success/no-findings result. The successful copied-template case supplies a concrete positive result in this review. | A writing requirement alone does not establish sustained reporting behavior. |
| Independent review and external consumers exposing misses | The review collection separates same-assignment repetition, varied questions, artifact-only reading, and external-consumer use; it asks for actual inherited context and preserved first judgments. This assignment could retain a distinct verdict. | I did not inspect or compare the other current reviews/consumer experiment, and cannot establish their independence or effectiveness. |
| Review as one method among many | Addressed at the guidance/entrypoint level: the general task collection routes to review as one option among other concrete moves. | Breadth of recipes is not proof each is equally useful. |
| Distinguishing public practice, history, rule-based design, and invention | The guides visibly label public adaptations and translated/combined historical questions; their evidence statements distinguish provenance from comparative effectiveness. | This review did not re-verify external sources or private historical translations. Labels are verified as labels, not as proof of fidelity or effectiveness. |
| Portability and ordinary adoption | Normal filled backend relocation/default product role passes; F2 and F3 expose remaining layout and profile gaps beyond the original changed examples. | No real independent project was migrated. |

| `python3 scripts/read_rules.py prepare` | 9 units, 92,501 body bytes, 97,685 transcript bytes; final completion marker. Initial tool output was truncated, partly because of my batching; I used complete digest-checked recovery instead of treating the manifest as reading. |

| `python3 scripts/read_rules.py prepare --concern experience --owner experience=docs/contracts/documentation-harness.md` | Exit 0, harness owner present, no graphical frontend unit forced. Relevant source text was read directly. |
| Actual filled/relocated backend template, then checker and state-integrity owner-bound preparation | Both exit 0. Omitted product role accepted. 11 prepared units include backend and copied owner; completion marker present. |
| Root-product/directory-product contrast | Root remains pass; directory source is reported and blocks. |
| Time/demo reader contrast | Both exit 0; time excludes the shared data-risk condition, demo whole-document fallback includes it. |
| Full working-tree unittest suite | 169 tests pass, 43.353 seconds. |
| Full working-tree documentation checker | Exit 0; 65 canonical documents, 16 templates, full profile, adopted stage; one overdue-promise advisory. |

The core's byte size is an observation, not a separate finding. Emit time is small, and I did not measure reader effort or establish a usability regression. My initial aggregate-output truncation should not be represented as an isolated defect of the reader CLI.

## Scope left open and stopping basis

The decisive probes answer the selected rule-delivery and portability questions and provide both working cases and countercases. I stop at the bounded review and hand the supported findings to the integration owner. I have not implemented repairs, changed Git state, modified rules/tests/plans/evidence in the repository, or started ongoing work.

Unresolved: actual independent-project adoption; long-term owner attention and executor performance; source fidelity of every transferred public/historical method; other language/layout combinations; real migration behavior; autonomous runtime integration; frontend rendering and interaction; production quality boundaries. The review therefore supports a clear improvement judgment plus three specific remaining issues, not whole-project completion assurance.

# First understanding — before producer-success comparison

Recorded at the start of this experiment, after receiving the delegated task and runtime instructions and reading the supplied AGENTS.md plus docs/README.md through its task-context and document-stock sections. No prior or current reviewer results, producing conversation, repository history, or top-level README purpose text has been read.

My initial understanding is that this repository is a collection of instructions for making an engineering agent's decisions and delivery reliable. It seems to emphasize knowing the desired observable result, respecting the person who owns decisions, grounding claims in evidence, and using documents as decision owners rather than treating document completion as the objective. Its entrypoint also tells me to activate detailed concerns when applicable and distinguishes learning the whole discipline from extracting one useful practice.

The most immediately useful idea I would take is to verify a promised result in both directions: test what was requested, then inspect what was actually produced for omissions and excess. I would use that outside this project because ordinary acceptance checklists can establish the intended output while missing an unintended effect or unsupported claim.

I have not yet read that rule's full owning section or its extraction instructions, so this is a preliminary interpretation from entrypoint language. I do not yet know whether the section is usable as a small independent practice or depends heavily on the rest of the discipline.

My provisional experiment is a small local document-delivery task using supplied facts: draft a release note and check that its promises and actual statements agree with the request and source facts. The disposable task has no external publication and no repository adoption. This avoids treating a successful checker run or filled policy file as a reader's successful use.

I have not yet assessed whether these ideas accurately represent the project's expressed purpose. That comparison will follow the extraction/use attempt.

report.text:
# Outside-agent takeaway experiment

## Verdict

**Supported positive result:** without the producing conversation, I understood a useful part of this project and applied it outside the checkout. I would retain the practice of checking both requested results and the actual delivered claims/effects. The selected text gave me an executable review method, not merely a form to fill.

The trial was deliberately small and synthetic. I authored its source facts and a candidate containing a known unsupported claim, then used the selected practice to repair the candidate. This establishes usable understanding in this context. It does not measure blind defect discovery, independent operator comprehension, sustained adoption, or the whole library's transfer quality. No substantial communication defect is established by this experiment.

The most important remaining limits are that a raw excerpt is not a complete standalone policy, task-specific authority and facts still have to come from the receiving task, and this trial cannot separate what the project taught from similar instructions and capabilities already present in my runtime.

## Assignment, authority, and boundary

The delegated assignment reports the owner's question as: what would an independent external agent take from this project, can it understand the intended message without the producing conversation, and what was not conveyed and why? I received no expected takeaway list or desired verdict. I was free to choose the practice, task and path and to revise my selection.

Authority was read-only source investigation and bounded local disposable use. Root owns integration and synthesis. No repository edits, commits, external publication, messages to third parties, private history access, other reviewer results, unrelated personal locations, neighboring project-script execution, or further agents were authorized. I kept those boundaries. The only project executable I ran was the explicitly required rule reader, `scripts/read_rules.py`; Python commands used `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`.

Paths in this record use `<source-checkout>` for the investigated repository and `<experiment-root>` for this uniquely generated disposable directory. Source locators are repository-relative. This directory is evidence for root's review and is disposable after evidence use; none of its artifacts is a product dependency.

## Actual context received

`fork_turns=none` excluded the parent's producing conversation. It did **not** create an empty runtime. My first understanding was influenced by these actual inputs:

- General system instructions identified an API assistant and supplied normal reasoning, safety and response rules.
- Codex developer instructions supplied autonomous execution, authorization boundaries, evidence/testing guidance, plain-language communication, tool-use rules and a skills catalog. They already favored verifying outcomes, preserving user authority and carrying work to completion. Tool descriptions and permission boundaries were present.
- The full repository working agreement was supplied as user-context AGENTS.md instructions, along with the checkout location, shell, date, timezone and writable roots. That agreement already named the observable outcome, ranked transfer values, pointed to bounded extraction, and explicitly required bidirectional verification.
- The parent supplied this bounded consumer assignment, its authority limits, a coordination locator and a warning not to confuse missing context or tools with communication failure. I did not receive the owner's original producing conversation, original private source records, earlier reviewer conclusions or current sibling results.
- The coordination surface was inspected only for its request/coordination section and heading locations. It confirmed separate read-only workers and root synthesis; I did not read its review-concern body or observations/synthesis body. I sent root a selection update and completion progress, without receiving another evaluator's judgment.

The runtime describes the assistant as Codex based on GPT-6. An exact underlying model identifier is not observable from these inputs. No model variation or second reader was used. No skill was invoked: the task used this repository's existing methods and local plain-text evidence, rather than a Word/PDF/Page deliverable or external application.

Consequently, “fresh” means independent of the producing conversation and other reviewers, not independent of all engineering guidance. The initial selection also came from normal project instructions already in context; it was not a claim that I invented the practice from an unbiased blank slate.

## First understanding and selection

`01-first-understanding.md` records my initial judgment before I assessed producer success or read the homepage's purpose. At that point I had received the supplied AGENTS.md and read `docs/README.md` through task context and document stock. I understood the repository as instructions for reliable engineering-agent decisions and delivery: know the observable result, preserve human decision ownership, ground claims in evidence, and use documents as rule owners rather than substitutes for the task.

I selected **bidirectional verification**, initially from AGENTS.md's verification instruction: test requested results, then inspect the actual result for omissions and excess. I would use it because a positive acceptance checklist can miss a false side claim or unintended effect. I retained that choice after the trial.

This was bounded extraction, not a request to learn or adopt every discipline. The initial record explicitly left open whether the complete rule would prove usable without importing the rest of the repository.

## Inspection path and source identities

The path followed the agent entrypoint rather than beginning with the homepage:

1. Supplied `AGENTS.md` → `docs/README.md#task-context`.
2. `scripts/read_rules.py list` and `docs/contracts/documentation-harness.md#complete-rule-delivery-is-a-read-only-transaction` to obtain the required core correctly.
3. `scripts/read_rules.py prepare` to a local transcript, followed by complete digest-checked source delivery. The first batched output truncated the middle of development-core part 2; I re-read that part completely with its expected digest before dependent work.
4. `docs/contracts/project-adoption.md#take-one-practice-into-an-authorized-task` and `docs/guides/project-operation.md#take-one-practice-into-a-task` for the selected extraction route.
5. `docs/contracts/agent-execution-discipline.md#parallel-work-is-coordinated-in-writing` and `#delegated-work-carries-bounded-context-and-returns-to-an-owner`, plus the coordination section only.
6. `docs/contracts/development-discipline.md#verify-promised-and-observed-behavior-in-both-directions` for the selected operative rule.
7. After completing the disposable use and recording its first result, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and the purpose/scope and transfer-value sections of `docs/contracts/project-adoption.md` for expressed-purpose comparison.

The required core comprised nine units and **92,501 bytes** of source text: authority order, language style, development core, governance core, execution profiles, risk, route, completion, and task context. `02-core-reading.txt` retains its manifest, source digests, full bodies and final aggregate completion marker. This is the actual reading burden of my governed source inspection, not a claim that an external target must adopt those units.

`05-source-artifact-identities.json` records whole-file SHA-256 identities and byte counts for every inspected source file or source-code file, including the partially inspected rule-reader implementation and coordination file. Hashing a whole file does not mean I semantically inspected its unselected body. The source identities used by core preparation were unchanged when rechecked at the end. The checkout already contained many unrelated tracked and untracked changes; I made none.

The carried package consists of exact source excerpts and a provenance manifest:

| Carried artifact | Source locator | Bytes |
|---|---|---:|
| `carried-material/bidirectional-verification.md` | `docs/contracts/development-discipline.md#verify-promised-and-observed-behavior-in-both-directions` | 4,822 |
| `carried-material/bounded-extraction.md` | `docs/contracts/project-adoption.md#take-one-practice-into-an-authorized-task` | 1,009 |
| `carried-material/extraction-operation-card.md` | `docs/guides/project-operation.md#take-one-practice-into-a-task` | 1,720 |

The exact excerpt digests and originating whole-file digests are in `carried-material/manifest.json`. There is no requirement to trust a current commit as the identity of uncommitted content.

## Disposable task and observed use

I chose a document review task, not a software implementation: produce a short release note for a fictional CSV export tool. `trial/task-and-facts.md` owns the local brief and synthetic source facts. It requires two changes—new exports report written-record count and delimiter errors identify the input file—plus a concrete recovery action. It forbids invented release metadata or unsupported claims. No publication or real application behavior was involved.

I supplied those task-specific inputs because the transferable practice cannot know a receiving project's intent or facts. The selected decision was whether the candidate note was ready to deliver.

`trial/candidate-note.txt` included all three positive requirements and deliberately added that every previous export had already been regenerated. The source facts said old exports were unchanged and no background regeneration occurred. This is a known adverse case, not an unknown defect discovered independently.

From the disposable directory I read only the carried material, local brief and candidate. I then:

1. Checked the candidate against the three promised results. All were present.
2. Enumerated the actual factual statements and mapped each back to the brief's facts. The added historical regeneration/count-availability promise was contradicted or unsupported. “Each export” also left the new-export scope implicit.
3. Removed the unsupported side promise and made the scope explicit.
4. Read the actual final text and confirmed it retained the requested changes and next action. I did not modify the task's source facts.

The actual final note is:

> New CSV exports report the number of records written when they complete. Delimiter errors identify the affected input file; select a comma-delimited file and retry.

`trial/review-observations.md` retains the forward and reverse mappings. `trial/trial-artifact-identities.json` identifies the brief, original candidate, observation record and final note. I did not reopen the source checkout between reading the carried material in the disposable directory and finishing this result. No checker, project template, dependency package, network access, build or application runtime was needed for this use.

A login shell emitted an incidental parse-error line while still displaying the complete local text and exiting successfully. Subsequent operations with `login=false` worked. This is a runtime-shell issue, not a demonstrated defect in the repository's communication.

## What transferred, and what did not

**The method transferred.** The rule specified a concrete second pass over actual effects absent from the expected list. Its identity/scope prompt was also applicable. That is why it could improve the final artifact even when the forward checklist was satisfied. The rule also made its own evidence limits explicit: inspect the actual claimed surface and do not promote missing observations into passes. The extraction card allowed a small receiving task to retain its own owner rather than copying the governance tree.

**The target facts and acceptance standard had to be supplied.** This is a necessary input boundary, not missing communication: the general practice should not invent a target project's requirements or truth. If those inputs had been unavailable, the trial would have been incomplete rather than a failed source explanation.

**The document-task mapping was my inference.** The rule talks primarily about owning contracts, scenarios and external effects. I treated factual sentences as effects at a reader boundary and the brief/facts file as this small task's existing owner. The extraction card's CLI/README example and retained core made that adaptation reasonable. The selected excerpt alone has not been tested by a new reader on that adaptation.

**Raw extraction did not preserve working navigation.** I copied three sections rather than their repository topology. A local link check found four repository-relative Markdown links whose package targets do not exist; `04-portable-link-observation.json` records them. The verification excerpt also retains source-anchor labels without their historical bodies. None was required to complete this trial, and the manifest preserved the original locators. This is an observed limit of my raw extraction package, not evidence that the source repository's links are broken or that a required procedural dependency was unavailable. A reader wanting those optional extensions or historical rationale must return to the source or deliberately carry them.

**The core was larger than the local use.** Governed work required 92,501 source bytes, while the carried method/route excerpts totaled 7,551 bytes and the local action needed only its own facts and a manual review. This is a measured difference between source-governed reading and minimum demonstrated use. I did not compare reader time or failure rates, so it is not proof that the required core prevents uptake.

**No provenance or adoption claim follows from the trial.** I did not examine private history, other review results, or the origin of every normative statement. The homepage's statement about use in the maintainer's projects remains a self-report for this experiment. I established that the current rule can be understood and used here; I did not establish its historical origin, unique novelty, production effectiveness or sustained reuse.

## Comparison with the expressed purpose

This comparison occurred after both `01-first-understanding.md` and `03-trial-first-result.md` were written.

`README.md` presents the project as a domain-neutral engineering discipline whose value lies in judgment and delivery, with documents and tools as carriers. It describes a longer-term institution for delegated agents, learning from failures, protecting owner attention, and requiring evidence for claims. `docs/contracts/project-adoption.md#transfer-value-is-ranked-before-its-carriers` ranks interaction/epistemic discipline, ownership/truth and coherent delivery above documentation tooling. `ARCHITECTURE.md` is explicitly an unconfigured adopting-project template, consistent with the homepage's statement that there is no product implementation.

My initial reading captured the judgment, authority, evidence and observable-outcome parts accurately. My selected practice lies within the expressed delivery/evidence value and did not confuse copying the checker with the desired benefit. The exact long-term institutional framing was not part of my first understanding; the normal AGENTS-led entry route gave operational rules first, and the homepage made that framing explicit later. The core's experience-reuse rules also communicated the failure-to-future-action idea before I read the homepage. This is delayed emphasis along my chosen route, not an idea absent from the project.

The trial supports a bounded answer to the owner's question: **an external agent without the producing conversation can understand an intended practice and use it successfully.** The text did not require reconstructing a private incident to execute this selected method. What remains unproved is wider independent uptake and whether a reader with fewer overlapping runtime instructions would reach the same understanding or make the same adaptation.

## Stopping basis and retained takeaway

The delegated end was reached: first understanding recorded; own selection retained; complete source and relevant dependencies obtained; one disposable use completed; actual result, dependencies, adaptation and evidence limits recorded; expressed purpose compared afterward. No full adoption, source repair or further review was undertaken.

I would retain this short cue at the receiving task's existing review point: **check every promised outcome, then enumerate the actual delivered claims/effects and map each back to authority, including scope and recovery. Keep unknowns visible.** That is my compact adaptation of the source, not a replacement normative owner for the template.

### Verify promised and observed behavior in both directions

The owning contract's acceptance matrix lists functional outcomes and activated
nonfunctional requirements by user or operator scenario. Each names a trigger,
starting state, observable response, and applicable boundary. Link an existing
quality owner instead of duplicating its threshold. Do not derive this list
solely from the tests or the implementation. The future reconciliation
`promise[...]` register is not a product feature inventory.

For effects such as requests, writes, events, notifications, or repeated user
actions, define the affected identity and scope, allowed count or bound per
logical operation, and relevant timing/order. Where repetition matters, also
define which triggers create an operation, any cadence or bound across an
observation window, and the freshness or maximum silence the outcome permits.
Include concurrency, retries, cache reuse, and suppression when they can
change those effects. State what is unknown; do not invent a safe request rate
or claim exactly-once behavior from
an idempotency key alone. User cost includes unnecessary requests, account
exposure, latency, attention, and recovery effort when applicable.

Verification runs in both directions:

- For each promised result, observe whether it occurs under its trigger and
  meets its functional and quality boundaries.
- Inspect actual externally visible effects at the affected boundary, including
  effects absent from the expected-result list. Map each to an authorized
  requirement or report it for reconciliation. Evidence drawn only from a
  helper's return value cannot establish effects at another boundary.
- Distinguish missing, undeclared, excessive, and wrongly suppressed effects.
  Also inspect wrong identity/scope, premature or stale effects, partial
  completion, and misleading success when applicable. These are prompts for
  analysis, not an exhaustive taxonomy or a mandatory test count.
- Exercise failure and recovery from the user's position: what is known, what
  remains unresolved, what was changed, and what action is available next.
- Never attribute a failure to the user's environment without evidence. A fix
  is verified in the environment where the failure was reported; reproducing
  a similar failure elsewhere establishes a hypothesis, not the fix. When a
  failure class will need cross-environment diagnosis, the product ships its
  own diagnostic surface instead of relying on the reporter's description.
- For material or high-risk user- or operator-facing delivery, acceptance
  includes a fresh-context consumer: an independent agent or reviewer who
  receives what a real consumer would have and uses the deliverable to its
  stated end. Routine mechanically bounded work with credible focused
  verification can close on that evidence, unless an activated owner or the
  explicit brief requires an independent consumer. For example, a bounded
  local list sort can use observed state, ordering and recovery checks; a
  material new workflow or reusable explanation needs the consumer trial.
  Investigate a failed trial at its artifact, supplied-input and environment
  boundaries before locating the defect. Missing inputs and failed execution
  remain incomplete evidence rather than a passing review or an automatic
  attribution of fault to the consumer.

Match the inspected object and scope to the claim: a source record, generated
summary, rendered main text, and whole collection expose different properties.
Record which was actually available and inspected. A schema review may need
the full record; a reader trial needs the actual reader surface. One cannot
silently stand in for the other. When a proposed fix changes hidden or unused
material, compare its effect at the claimed boundary before crediting it with
improving that outcome.

When results depend on a catalog, classifier, parser, or filter, inspect what
was unmatched, rejected, or omitted before interpreting an empty result as
success. Lack of a known match is not evidence that no problem exists. Preserve
the owning contract's policy for unknown and partial results; do not silently
invent an answer or suppress the unresolved case to keep the result clean.

Use the smallest credible evidence for each claim. A failing regression test,
an instrumented process, a packaged artifact, a browser observation, or a
bounded manual review may be appropriate. Record the relevant conditions and
limits. Missing observations remain unknown or not run, never a pass. Required
evidence for a completion claim cannot be replaced by a cheaper unrelated check.

### Take one practice into an authorized task

A request to inspect the template or take a useful practice can select a
bounded extraction. Start with the target task, its current authority and the
specific decision the practice should improve. Obtain that practice's complete
operative owner and applicable dependencies, try it at the relevant boundary,
and carry its conditions and evidence limits with the result. The
[operation card](../guides/project-operation.md#take-one-practice-into-a-task)
provides a small worked route.

Finish with the recommendation, authorized trial or retained change the owner
requested. Keep existing target instructions and rule owners. This route
neither requires a full-library survey nor claims one, and it does not itself
authorize copying the governance tree, changing product behavior or enabling
enforcement. A later request to learn the discipline in full takes the survey
below; work governed by this template still obtains its required core and
activated detail.

extraction-operation-card.md.text:
### Take one practice into a task

Use this card for [bounded extraction](../contracts/project-adoption.md#take-one-practice-into-an-authorized-task),
such as taking a review question or recovery method into an existing project.
Full learning and formal adoption keep their own broader routes.

1. Name the current task, the useful change and its sufficient stopping point.
2. Inspect the target's facts, existing rule owner and authorization. Choose
   one practice that improves an actual decision in that task.
3. Read its complete operative source and applicable dependencies. Carry the
   conditions that make it useful, including the case where it should not run.
4. Try it inside the authorized task and inspect the actual result and effects.
   State an untested proposal as a proposal; use focused evidence for a small task.
5. When retention is requested, put the useful result at the target's existing
   owner or next matching entrypoint, with the reason to revalidate it.

For example, a small CLI can keep its README as behavior owner and take the
method of checking failure channels, corrected-input retry and an unreported
sibling error. It can finish when that bounded behavior is observed. Copying
the template's checker or document tree is a separate adoption choice.

Use the [practical task CheatSheet](task-cheatsheet.md) to select or construct a
useful move, including the specialized [review collection](review-cheatsheet.md).
Rules specify the boundary; the task SOP orders the work; a CheatSheet helps
choose an effective action inside it.
Work governed by this template still obtains its global core and activated
detail. The card is a method entrypoint, not a replacement for those sources.

# Local task and facts

This is a synthetic document review and repair exercise. I authored the brief, the facts and the initial candidate, and I deliberately included one unsupported side claim. It is a known adverse case for demonstrating an executable review procedure, not blind discovery of an unknown defect.

Task: produce one short plain-text release note for operators of a fictional CSV export tool. Describe the two supported changes and the next action after the delimiter error. The source facts below are the task's authority. Do not publish the note, add a release date/version, invent a performance claim, or modify the source facts.

Source facts:
- A newly requested export reports the number of records actually written when it completes.
- Invalid delimiters produce an error naming the affected input file.
- Recovery is to select a comma-delimited file and retry the export. The invalid input is preserved.
- Previously created exports are unchanged. No background regeneration occurs.

Sufficient local result: a concise final note contains the two changes and recovery action, and every factual claim in that final note is supported by these facts. The final delivery is its actual plain-text content. No claim about a real application's behavior is being tested.

Containment: all artifacts live in this disposable trial directory, with no network or external publication. Abort if a step would read or write unrelated locations or require the source checkout to be changed. Scratch artifacts are retained as experiment evidence for root synthesis, not production dependencies; disposable cleanup is limited to this uniquely owned directory after evidence use.

# Review observations from the disposable task

This is the same agent/context that read the source and authored the synthetic candidate. It is not a second cold reader or independent defect discovery. The actual task boundary is the wording delivered to an operator, not an executing CSV export application.

## Forward check against requested results

| Promised result | Candidate evidence | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Describe record-count reporting on a new export | First sentence describes count at completion | Present, though “each export” leaves the new-export scope implicit |
| Describe file-identifying delimiter errors | Second sentence identifies the affected input file | Present |
| Give recovery action | Second sentence says to select a comma-delimited file and retry | Present |

A checklist consisting only of those three positive requirements would mark this candidate complete.

## Reverse check of the actual delivered statements

| Actual statement | Source support or conflict | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Export completion shows records written | Supported for newly requested exports only | Say “New CSV exports” to make the identity/scope explicit |
| Delimiter errors name the affected input file | Supported | Retain |
| Select a comma-delimited file and retry | Supported recovery action | Retain |
| All previously created exports have already been regenerated | Contradicts the source fact that previous exports are unchanged and no regeneration occurs | Remove |
| Counts are immediately available for previous exports | Unsupported consequence of the preceding false claim | Remove |

The selected rule supplied the instruction to inspect actual claims beyond the expected-result list and to check identity/scope. I supplied the document-task interpretation that a factual sentence is an effect at the reader boundary; the source rule does not give this specific release-note mapping.

The final note makes its new-export scope explicit and removes the unsupported history/regeneration promise. All requested content remains. No source facts changed. I inspected the actual final text, not a helper return value or a claim that a checker passed. The next reader action after a delimiter error is explicit.

This establishes that I can apply the carried practice to one small document task without reopening the source checkout. It does not establish real software behavior, actual operator comprehension, automatic detection of false claims, independent review, long-term recall, or full-library learning.

from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import tomllib

root = Path('<source-checkout>')
record_path = Path('<temporary-directory>/2026-10-29-template-wide-root-checks.json')
out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='template-wide-root-followup-', dir='<temporary-directory>'))
env = {**os.environ, 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE': '1'}
record = {
    'method': 'Parent independently reran source-level probes after reading reviewer two. Fixtures are data copies, not new project adoptions. Product text is never executed.',
    'scope': 'Current working tree; no canonical rule, implementation, template or test changes.',
    'cases': [],
}

def run(name, args, cwd):
    start = time.monotonic()
    result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, *args], cwd=cwd, env=env,
                            capture_output=True, timeout=180)
    (out / (name + '.stdout.txt')).write_bytes(result.stdout)
    (out / (name + '.stderr.txt')).write_bytes(result.stderr)
    case = {'name': name, 'arguments': args, 'exit_code': result.returncode,
            'seconds': round(time.monotonic() - start, 3),
            'stdout_bytes': len(result.stdout), 'stderr_bytes': len(result.stderr),
            'stdout_sha256': hashlib.sha256(result.stdout).hexdigest(),
            'stderr_sha256': hashlib.sha256(result.stderr).hexdigest()}
    record['cases'].append(case)
    print(json.dumps({k: case[k] for k in ['name', 'exit_code', 'seconds']}), flush=True)
    return result, case

fixture = out / 'snapshot'
source_digests = {}
try:
    risk_condition = 'stop and obtain a human data-risk decision.'
    for concern in ['time-and-calendar', 'demonstration-data']:
        result, case = run(concern, ['scripts/read_rules.py', 'prepare', '--concern', concern], root)
        text = result.stdout.decode()
        manifest = json.loads(text.splitlines()[1])
        case.update({'units': [u['identity'] for u in manifest['units']],
                     'sources': manifest['sources'],
                     'final_marker': text.splitlines()[-1],
                     'contains_time_data_risk_condition': risk_condition in text})

    names = subprocess.run(['git', 'ls-files', '--cached', '--others', '--exclude-standard', '-z'],
                           cwd=root, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout.decode().split('\0')
    for name in sorted(set(filter(None, names))):
        source = root / name
        if not source.is_file():
            continue
        data = source.read_bytes()
        source_digests[name] = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        target = fixture / name
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_bytes(data)

    record['source_digests'] = source_digests
    for name in ['main.py', 'app/main.py']:
        if (fixture / name).exists():
            raise RuntimeError('Fixture would overwrite an existing file: ' + name)

    result, case = run('unchanged-fixture', ['scripts/check_docs.py'], fixture)
    case['output'] = (result.stdout + result.stderr).decode()
    product_text = b'def main():\n    return "fixture application"\n\nif __name__ == "__main__":\n    print(main())\n'
    (fixture / 'main.py').write_bytes(product_text)
    result, case = run('root-application', ['scripts/check_docs.py'], fixture)
    case['output'] = (result.stdout + result.stderr).decode()
    (fixture / 'app').mkdir()
    (fixture / 'main.py').rename(fixture / 'app/main.py')
    result, case = run('directory-application', ['scripts/check_docs.py'], fixture)
    case['output'] = (result.stdout + result.stderr).decode()
    shutil.rmtree(fixture / 'app')
    record['product_text_sha256'] = hashlib.sha256(product_text).hexdigest()

    policy_path = fixture / 'docs-policy.toml'
    policy_text = policy_path.read_text()
    policy = tomllib.loads(policy_text)
    if policy_text.count('profile = "full"') != 1:
        raise RuntimeError('Unexpected profile input')
    optional = policy['templates']['tiers']['standard'] + policy['templates']['tiers']['full']
    for name in optional:
        (fixture / 'templates' / name).unlink()
    policy_path.write_text(policy_text.replace('profile = "full"', 'profile = "minimal"'))
    record['minimal_only_changes'] = {'profile': 'full -> minimal', 'removed_templates': optional}
    result, case = run('minimal-checker', ['scripts/check_docs.py'], fixture)
    case['output'] = (result.stdout + result.stderr).decode()
    result, case = run('minimal-prescribed-suite', ['-m', 'unittest', 'discover', '-s', 'tests', '-p', 'test_*.py'], fixture)
    combined = (result.stdout + result.stderr).decode()
    case['summary'] = [line for line in combined.splitlines()
                       if re.match(r'^(Ran \d+ tests|FAILED|OK|FAIL:|ERROR:)', line)]
    record['source_changes_during_probe'] = [name for name, digest in source_digests.items()
        if not (root / name).is_file() or hashlib.sha256((root / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() != digest]
finally:
    if fixture.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(fixture)
    record['fixture_removed'] = not fixture.exists()
    (out / 'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + '\n')
    existing = json.loads(record_path.read_text())
    existing['reviewer_two_followup'] = record
    record_path.write_text(json.dumps(existing, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + '\n')
    print('Results retained in ' + str(out), flush=True)

---
doc_type: evidence
status: historical
authority: evidence
last_reconciled: 2026-10-29
subject: independent-template-review-and-external-transfer
---

# Independent template review and external transfer

## Request and coordination

The owner requested two independent subagents with the same review assignment
to check whether earlier problems remain, and a third independent agent to
decide what it would take from this template, try using it, and investigate
what the project fails to communicate outside its producing context.

This is a bounded review. Root owns synthesis and source-level verification;
the three workers are read-only apart from uniquely owned disposable probes
and reports outside the repository. Current rules, guides, harness, templates
and earlier work remain unchanged during this round. Review findings do not
themselves authorize their implementation.

`template_review_one` and `template_review_two` received the identical brief,
whose original SHA-256 is
`fdbc2618c61c05562a5c023ac62e9b124e980faab0bd95778dbc737f884d2bfa`.
`outside_takeaway` received a separate consumer task without an expected
takeaway list or earlier verdicts. All three used `fork_turns=none`, excluding
the producing conversation. Workers did not see each other's current results.
Their actual inherited instructions and evidence origins are recorded below.

## Baseline and scope

The inspected baseline is the current working tree based on
`fa01192f094585ff0c1aaa6942ac04e63a11983a`, including its existing tracked and
untracked changes. The complete-rule core remains nine units. The review
considers the template as a whole, including normal use and missing outcomes,
with earlier owner concerns as context rather than a fixed defect checklist.

The review brief addressed abstraction and practical execution, complete
activated detail, mission and outcome preservation, positive supported
judgment, genuine review independence, task methods beyond review, and honest
method provenance. The consumer chose its own takeaway through normal project
entrypoints. Root preserved first judgments, investigated unique and conflicting
findings, and distinguished native context separation from independent source
evidence or an empty runtime.

## Judgment

The template has become materially more usable. It communicates observable
outcomes, decision ownership and evidence, offers a concrete task procedure,
and supplies practical methods beyond review. A fresh consumer selected and
used one intended practice outside the checkout. These are supported gains.

Four P2 defects remain in complete rule delivery and ordinary adoption paths.
Root independently reproduced all four. The most direct continuation of the
owner's earlier concern is an applicable exception omitted by the declared
Time reading unit. Correctly delivering a selected unit still does not prove
that its boundary carries the complete applicable rule. The adoption
countercases likewise expose promised uses that the normal passing suite does
not exercise end to end.

The two identical assignments produced different findings: reviewer one found
the newline defect; reviewer two found the other three. Synthesis preserves
all four rather than requiring agreement. This round demonstrates additional
coverage from these separate inspection paths; it does not establish that
same-task replication is always the most effective review method.

The [observation record](2026-10-29-template-wide-review-observations.json)
preserves both first verdicts, both full reports, the consumer's first
understanding and report, relevant source identities, probe results, the
complete small consumer trial, and root's reproductions. First judgments are
unchanged. Host-specific paths in other records are normalized with original
byte identities retained. Verbose repeated rule bodies and full failing-suite
logs are not duplicated.

## Findings verified by root

### F1 — P2 — The Time unit excludes an applicable recovery condition

The current [runtime contract](../contracts/foundational-runtime-discipline.md)
closes its Time unit at line 225. Lines 327–330 separately require a human
data-risk decision when stored timestamps were naive or were rewritten by a
timezone change. No explicit dependency carries that condition into the Time
unit's closure.

Root ran the actual reader against the unchanged sources:

| Preparation | Exit | Final marker | Data-risk condition delivered |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `prepare --concern time-and-calendar` | 0 | `READING COMPLETE units=10` | No |
| `prepare --concern demonstration-data` | 0 | `READING COMPLETE units=10` | Yes, through whole-document fallback |

The reader follows its declaration; the defect is the semantic boundary of the
declared rule. A worker repairing historical timestamps can obtain every
selected byte yet miss the domain-specific intervention condition. Generic
governance can still require owner involvement, and reading the whole file
catches the condition. No data repair or actual harm was observed. The
consequence is a reproducible gap in the complete-activated-detail promise.

### F2 — P2 — CRLF metadata prevents normal rule delivery

The [metadata parser](../../scripts/rule_reading.py), lines 17–19, recognizes
only LF delimiters while its caller decodes original bytes without newline
normalization. Root held the source content and reader fixed:

| Newline variant | Exit | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| LF | 0 | Nine units and completion marker |
| All CRLF | 1 | Missing frontmatter; no emitted rules |
| CRLF only in development metadata | 1 | Same failure |
| CRLF only in development body | 0 | Nine units and completion marker |

Reviewer one also reproduced the failure with an actual local Git
`core.autocrlf=true` checkout. This is Git conversion observed on macOS, not a
Windows-runtime trial. The repository has no Markdown LF checkout rule.
Direct complete reading remains a working fallback; real-adopter frequency
is unknown. Any repair needs to preserve original-byte identity and rule
output while recognizing equivalent metadata delimiters.

### F3 — P2 — Documented minimal adoption breaks the prescribed suite

The [README](../../README.md), lines 133–135, allows selecting the minimal
profile and deleting higher-tier templates. The [tests guidance](../../tests/README.md)
asks adopters to keep the suite, and the [CI example](../../templates/ci/docs-check.example.yml)
runs it. Tests unconditionally read optional live templates and assume the
policy still contains `profile = "full"`; see
[reader fixtures](../../tests/test_read_rules.py), lines 64–71 and 348–379,
and [checker fixtures](../../tests/test_check_docs.py), lines 34–48 and 877–918.

Root copied the current tree into an isolated fixture, changed only the
profile to minimal, and removed exactly the twelve standard/full templates:

| Prescribed command | Observed result |
|---|---|
| `python3 scripts/check_docs.py` | Exit 0; four templates, minimal profile |
| `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` | Exit 1; 169 tests, eight failures and eighteen errors |

This independently matches reviewer two's result. The unchanged full tree
passes all 169 tests. The portability defect is that valid adopter choices
also damage the inherited infrastructure's test baseline. The promised small
adoption therefore needs unadvertised fixture maintenance or retention of
optional templates. Hosted CI and an independent real-project migration were
not run. Root removed its fixture and verified source digests were unchanged.

### F4 — P2 — A root-only application escapes source-scope detection

The [checker](../../scripts/check_docs.py), lines 1518–1520, exempts every
root-level file. The current policy and harness prose explicitly specify
this exemption to accommodate tooling. It is a design blind spot in that
exception, rather than an implementation that contradicts its narrow rule.

With the shipped adopted stage, `source_roots = ["src"]`, unconfigured
architecture and no product contract, root observed:

| Fixture | Exit | Observation |
|---|---:|---|
| Unchanged template | 0 | Baseline advisory only |
| Add application text as `main.py` | 0 | Exactly the same checker output |
| Move identical text to `app/main.py` | 1 | Unclaimed source reported |

No application text was executed. The exception uses position as a substitute
for identifying tooling, hiding the entirety of this ordinary single-file
application from the otherwise useful outside-root guard. Manual inventory
and architecture/contract duties still apply; a passing checker grants no
authority. Deliberately configured root scope was not tested and is not
claimed impossible. The fixture omitted Git metadata and was not a completed
adoption.

## Earlier concerns and present status

| Owner concern | Current judgment | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Many abstractions, little practical execution | Substantially improved: the operation guide gives a request-to-result procedure and worked decisions; the general CheatSheet covers diagnosis, inquiry, delivery, explanation, continuity, learning and simplification. | Findable, intelligible actions are observed; comparative effectiveness of every recipe is not. |
| Meta-rules substituting for complete detail | Partly improved: actual core bodies, owner binding and digest-checked recovery work on LF input; a relocated backend template obtains its complete backend unit. F1 and F2 leave substantive gaps. | Delivery and recovery are observable; understanding and application require separate evidence. |
| Mission reduced to metrics or process completion | Current owners preserve original request, accepted interpretation, actual effects and named end. The consumer chose a practice serving judgment and delivery rather than copying tooling. | Sustained prioritization and owner benefit in another project remain unmeasured. |
| Endless prohibitions without supported judgment | Language and Grill permit a supported pass and sufficient stopping point; all three agents independently named working parts and limits. | This bounded round shows the behavior, not a long-term rate. |
| Producer framing constraining review | Reviewers chose separate paths under identical open assignments; distinct findings and first verdicts survived integration. | Supplied owner-goal renderings and the same repository remain shared inputs; model diversity is unknown. |
| Treating review as the whole practical layer | The task collection now offers multiple task families, with review as one specialization. | Breadth is present; universal coverage or superiority is not established. |
| Unclear origins of practical methods | Public adaptations, translated/combined historical questions, rule-based design and effectiveness limits are visibly distinguished. | This round inspected those distinctions, not every public original or private historical record. |

Reviewer one's initial source-routing judgment was favorable within its
inspected LF cases. Reviewer two's Time counterexample narrows the combined
claim: complete emitted bodies and recovery work, while semantic dependency
closure remains incomplete. Root retains the original verdict rather than
rewriting it to make the reviews appear unanimous.

## What the outside agent actually took away

The third agent independently chose **bidirectional verification**: check the
requested results, then enumerate actual claims/effects and trace each back
to intent, facts and authority, including scope and recovery. Its first
understanding correctly identified engineering judgment, human ownership,
evidence and observable outcomes as the project's purpose. This choice fits
the project's stated transfer value order.

It carried three exact excerpts totaling 7,551 bytes and used them in a
disposable release-note task without reopening the source during that use.
The synthetic candidate contained all three requested items but also claimed
that historical exports had been regenerated. The supplied facts contradicted
that side claim. A forward requirements pass accepted the three requested
items; the reverse pass removed the false historical promise and made the
new-export scope explicit. Root inspected the brief, facts, candidate,
claim mapping and actual final text.

This is positive evidence of usable understanding. The agent authored the
facts and deliberately adverse candidate itself: it is a controlled
demonstration, not blind discovery of an unknown defect or a second reader's
comprehension test.

Observed transfer friction and limits have different meanings:

- Four relative links did not resolve after raw sections were copied into a
  flat package; source-anchor labels also lacked their historical bodies.
  None was needed for the trial. This is a packaging limitation of the chosen
  extraction, not broken source links or a demonstrated missing mandatory
  dependency.
